newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - outperformed by Treasuries.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - outperformed by Treasuries.

text.p: U.S. municipals in late trade Friday were up 3/8 to a 1/4 of a point, as positive news on inflation pulled prices higher, though not as strongly as Treasuries, which looked likely to keep outperforming.
"We're starting to have some coupon problems in municipals, prices are running up to the coupon level in a lot of cases," a trader said.

With less potential for further gains, and concerns that the yield offered by municipals when compared with Treasuries now stands about as low as it was likely to go, traders said municipal prices might stagnate even if their sister bonds keep rising.
"We're at pretty rich ratios to Treasuries," a trader said. "Our market is going to have a tougher time performing."
The latest economic reports have strengthened fixed-income markets, as they have depicted a slowing economy and easing inflation.

For example, a closely watched measure of wholesale inflation, the Producer Price Index fell in May, shedding 0.3 percent both overall and in the core rate, which excludes food and energy prices. The Labor Department said this was the first time in 45 years that wholesale prices declined for five consecutive months.

This has prompted widespread speculation that the Federal Reserve will not raise interest rates when its policy making arm meets in early July, but that expectation could get knocked for a loop if next week's Consumer Price Index for May failed to back it up.
"I guess the CPI is going to determine whether the Fed is going to do anything as far as rates go," a trader said.
The important measure of retail inflation, which was due out on June 17, was projected to show a 0.2 percent increase, after rising 0.1 percent in April, according to economists polled by Reuters.

While the municipal market was expected to keep getting the benefit of a huge increase in redemptions in June and July, supplies of new issues also were projected to stay strong, at least over the near-term.
Municipal bond sales for next week were expected to total $4.3 billion in 160 deals, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
Negotiated offerings totaled $3.2 billion in 73 sales, the largest total this year, with a $275 million Detroit Sewer Authority, Mich., deal through PaineWebber Inc. topping the list.
On the competitive side, 87 sales totaling $1.1 billion were scheduled. A $200 million Massachusettes Bay Transportation Authority deal on Wednesday was the largest.
Traders noted that while there was two-way trade, sellers were emerging with fairly aggressive numbers.
In the secondary market, Dallas-Fort Worth, Texas, Regulatory Airport Revenues of 2023, which pay a 5-1/2 percent coupon, were bid at 5.65 percent, NET, down four basis points.
And Dade County, Florida, Water and Sewer System Revenues of 2021, which pay a 5-1/4 percent coupon, were bid at 5.48 percent, NET, down eight basis points.

September Treasury bond futures ended up 15 ticks at 111-27/32, while September municipal bond futures gained 10 ticks to 117-26/32. This left the MOB spread between the two futures contracts at plus 191 ticks, slightly lower than levels seen earlier this week.
